source.text: Ἐλθὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὰ μέρη Καισαρείας τῆς Φιλίππου ἠρώτα τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγων· Τίνα λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;

records.literal_gloss: Having come then Jesus into the parts of Caesarea of Philip he was asking the disciples of him saying, Whom do say the men to be the Son of the Man?

en.L: Now when Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was asking {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, saying, "Who do {{gender:people|men}} say the Son of Man is?"
en.B: When Jesus reached the district around Caesarea Philippi, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put a question to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples: "Who do people say that the Son of Man is?"
en.R: Jesus went to the area near the town of Caesarea Philippi. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Who do people say the Son of Man is?"

es.L: Y habiendo llegado Jesús a la región de Cesarea de Filipo, preguntaba a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, diciendo: «¿Quién {{gender:dice la gente|dicen los hombres}} que es el Hijo del Hombre?».
es.B: Cuando Jesús llegó a la región de Cesarea de Filipo, hizo una pregunta a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿Quién dice la gente que es el Hijo del Hombre?».
es.R: Jesús fue a la zona cercana a la ciudad de Cesarea de Filipo. Allí preguntó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿Quién dice la gente que es el Hijo del Hombre?».

fr.L: Or Jésus, étant venu dans la région de Césarée de Philippe, interrogeait {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, disant : « Qui les {{gender:gens|hommes}} disent-ils être le Fils de l’homme ? »
fr.B: Lorsque Jésus arriva dans la région de Césarée de Philippe, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} posa cette question à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Au dire des gens, qui est le Fils de l’homme ? »
fr.R: Jésus est allé dans la région de la ville de Césarée de Philippe. Là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a demandé à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « D’après les gens, qui est le Fils de l’homme ? »

sw.L: Na Yesu alipofika katika sehemu za Kaisaria Filipi, alikuwa akiwauliza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akisema, "Watu wanasema kwamba Mwana wa Adamu ni nani?"
sw.B: Yesu alipofika katika eneo la Kaisaria Filipi, aliwauliza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} swali: "Watu husema kwamba Mwana wa Adamu ni nani?"
sw.R: Yesu alikwenda katika eneo lililo karibu na mji wa Kaisaria Filipi. Huko aliwauliza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Watu wanasema Mwana wa Adamu ni nani?"

vi.L: Và khi Đức Giê-xu đến miền Sê-sa-rê Phi-líp, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rằng: "Người ta nói Con Người là ai?"
vi.B: Khi Đức Giê-xu đến vùng Sê-sa-rê Phi-líp, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi các môn đồ: "Người ta nói Con Người là ai?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đi đến vùng gần thị trấn Sê-sa-rê Phi-líp. Ở đó {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi các môn đồ: "Người ta nói Con Người là ai?"

ko.L: 그런데 예수께서 빌립보 가이사랴 지방에 이르셨을 때, 자기 제자들에게 물으시며 말씀하셨다. "사람들이 인자를 누구라고 말하느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 빌립보 가이사랴 지방에 이르셨을 때, 제자들에게 물으셨다. "사람들은 인자를 누구라고 하느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 빌립보 가이사랴라는 도시 근처 지방으로 가셨다. 거기서 예수께서 제자들에게 물으셨다. "사람들은 인자, 곧 사람의 아들을 누구라고 하느냐?"

am.L: ኢየሱስም ወደ ቂሣርያ ፊልጶስ ክፍሎች በመጣ ጊዜ ደቀ መዛሙርቱን እንዲህ እያለ ይጠይቃቸው ነበር፦ «ሰዎች የሰውን ልጅ ማን ነው ይሉታል?»
am.B: ኢየሱስ ቂሣርያ ፊልጶስ ወደምትባለው አካባቢ በደረሰ ጊዜ ደቀ መዛሙርቱን እንዲህ ብሎ ጠየቃቸው፦ «ሰዎች የሰው ልጅ ማን ነው ይላሉ?»
am.R: ኢየሱስ ቂሣርያ ፊልጶስ በምትባል ከተማ አቅራቢያ ወዳለው አካባቢ ሄደ። በዚያም ደቀ መዛሙርቱን እንዲህ ብሎ ጠየቃቸው፦ «ሰዎች የሰው ልጅ ማን ነው ይላሉ?»

decisions.choice: Caesarea Philippi: a town in the far north, near the sources of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Herod's son Philip rebuilt the town and named it for the emperor; "Philippi" set it apart from Caesarea on the Mediterranean coast. It lay at the foot of Mount Hermon in a mostly Gentile region.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus speaks of himself
decisions.reason: Jesus uses this title for himself (8:20; 12:40), and the next question asks the disciples who he is (16:15).

decisions.choice: Who do people say the Son of Man is?, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Who do people say that I, the Son of Man, am?, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "I" (in the Greek, "me"), making plain that Jesus means himself. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: {{gender:dice la gente|dicen los hombres}}
decisions.reason: As the English Literal offers "people" or "men". The span takes in the verb, because "la gente" is singular and "los hombres" plural. Balanced and Readable say "la gente", as the English does.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre, with capitals and no gender setting
decisions.reason: The title used through Matthew, as in John: Jesus speaks of himself (meaning decision m2), so it is never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic present kept at Literal (16:15 "Il leur dit")
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers now meet stories. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level.

decisions.choice: les disciples at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: English Readable says "followers"; French "disciple" is a common, transparent word, and the style guide keeps "les disciples" at every level, as in Mark's French. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili title, as in John; "Adamu" is also a word for humankind (as in "binadamu"). "Mwana wa Mtu" is more literal but unfamiliar. Never under the gender setting. For review by a native speaker.

decisions.choice: watu, with no gender setting; deity_pronoun only on wake
alternatives: a gender span as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: Swahili "watu" already means people, men and women, so the setting has nothing to change. The deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives ("wake"), since a verb prefix cannot take a capital; Swahili has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: "Sê-sa-rê Phi-líp"
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliteration, as in Mark 8:27.

decisions.choice: "người ta" with no gender span; "Con Người" capitalised
decisions.reason: "Người ta" already takes in men and women. "Con Người" is a title and never takes the gender setting.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 16:13-28; "사람들" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so respect for Jesus is carried by -시- and 께서 (style guide, sections 4 and 7); Korean "사람" already includes men and women.

decisions.choice: "빌립보 가이사랴"; "인자" at every level, with "곧 사람의 아들" once (R)
decisions.reason: The Protestant form used in the Korean Mark 8:27. "인자" is the title in the Korean Gospels, explained once in the passage at Readable, never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; "ሰዎች" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Amharic and the passage carries no deity_pronoun spans. "ሰዎች" (people) already means men and women, so the gender setting has nothing to choose between either; the same holds for generic "ሰው" through the passage.

decisions.choice: "ደቀ መዛሙርት" at every level
alternatives: "ተከታዮች" (followers) at Readable, as the English Readable
decisions.reason: "ደቀ መዛሙርት" is the living Amharic word for a teacher's disciples and is understood by all readers, so Readable keeps it rather than switching to "ተከታዮች".

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οἱ μὲν Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, ἄλλοι δὲ Ἠλίαν, ἕτεροι δὲ Ἰερεμίαν ἢ ἕνα τῶν προφητῶν.

records.literal_gloss: They and said, Some indeed John the Baptist, others but Elijah, others but Jeremiah or one of the prophets.

en.L: And they said, "Some [say] John the Baptist, and others Elijah, and others Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
en.B: They replied, "Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; still others, Jeremiah or another of the prophets."
en.R: They answered, "Some people say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are John the Baptist. Others say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are Elijah. And others say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are Jeremiah or one of the other prophets."

es.L: Y ellos dijeron: «Unos, Juan el Bautista; otros, Elías; y otros, Jeremías o uno de los profetas».
es.B: Ellos respondieron: «Unos dicen que Juan el Bautista; otros, que Elías; y otros, que Jeremías o alguno de los profetas».
es.R: Ellos contestaron: «Algunos dicen que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres Juan el Bautista. Otros dicen que eres Elías. Y otros dicen que eres Jeremías o alguno de los otros profetas».

fr.L: Et ils dirent : « Les uns, Jean le Baptiste ; d’autres, Élie ; d’autres encore, Jérémie ou l’un des prophètes. »
fr.B: Ils répondirent : « Pour certains, Jean le Baptiste ; pour d’autres, Élie ; pour d’autres encore, Jérémie ou un autre prophète. »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Certains disent que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es Jean le Baptiste. D’autres disent que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es Élie. Et d’autres disent que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es Jérémie ou un des autres prophètes. »

sw.L: Nao wakasema, "Wengine [husema] Yohana Mbatizaji, na wengine Eliya, na wengine Yeremia au mmoja wa manabii."
sw.B: Walijibu, "Wengine husema ni Yohana Mbatizaji; wengine husema ni Eliya; na wengine, Yeremia au mmoja wa manabii."
sw.R: Walimjibu, "Watu wengine husema {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Yohana Mbatizaji. Wengine husema ni Eliya. Na wengine husema ni Yeremia au mmoja wa manabii wengine."

vi.L: Và họ thưa: "Có người [nói là] Giăng Báp-tít, có người [nói là] Ê-li, có người [nói là] Giê-rê-mi hoặc một trong các nhà tiên tri."
vi.B: Họ thưa: "Có người nói là Giăng Báp-tít, có người nói là Ê-li, còn những người khác nói là Giê-rê-mi hay một trong các nhà tiên tri."
vi.R: Họ trả lời: "Có người nói Thầy là Giăng Báp-tít. Người khác nói Thầy là Ê-li. Còn có người nói Thầy là Giê-rê-mi hay một trong các nhà tiên tri khác."

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 말했다. "어떤 사람들은 세례자 요한이라고 [하고], 다른 사람들은 엘리야라고, 또 다른 사람들은 예레미야나 예언자들 가운데 하나라고 [합니다]."
ko.B: 그들이 대답했다. "세례자 요한이라고 하는 사람들도 있고, 엘리야라고 하는 사람들도 있고, 예레미야나 예언자 가운데 한 분이라고 하는 사람들도 있습니다."
ko.R: 제자들이 대답했다. "어떤 사람들은 주님을 세례자 요한이라고 합니다. 엘리야라고 하는 사람들도 있습니다. 또 예레미야나 다른 예언자 가운데 한 분이라고 하는 사람들도 있습니다."

am.L: እነርሱም አሉ፦ «አንዳንዶች መጥምቁ ዮሐንስ [ነው ይላሉ]፣ ሌሎች ደግሞ ኤልያስ፣ ሌሎችም ኤርምያስ ወይም ከነቢያት አንዱ [ነው ይላሉ]።»
am.B: እነርሱም እንዲህ ብለው መለሱ፦ «አንዳንዶች መጥምቁ ዮሐንስ ነው ይላሉ፤ ሌሎች ኤልያስ ነው ይላሉ፤ ሌሎች ደግሞ ኤርምያስ ወይም ከነቢያት አንዱ ነው ይላሉ።»
am.R: እነርሱም እንዲህ ብለው መለሱለት፦ «አንዳንድ ሰዎች አንተ መጥምቁ ዮሐንስ ነህ ይላሉ። ሌሎች ኤልያስ ነህ ይላሉ። ሌሎች ደግሞ ኤርምያስ ወይም ከሌሎቹ ነቢያት አንዱ ነህ ይላሉ።»

decisions.choice: John the Baptist: John come back to life
decisions.reason: Herod Antipas thought this (14:1-2).

decisions.choice: Elijah: the prophet God promised to send before the day of the Lord
alternatives: Elijah only as a great prophet of the past
decisions.reason: Malachi 3:23-24 (4:5-6 in most translations) promised Elijah's return. Jesus said John was that Elijah (11:14).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah: the prophet of suffering and judgment
decisions.reason: Only Matthew names Jeremiah here. Why people thought of him is not said; he too warned of the temple's fall and was rejected by his own people.

decisions.choice: say you are
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the words the Greek leaves understood.

decisions.choice: Unos, Juan el Bautista, with no bracketed verb
decisions.reason: Spanish can leave out the verb after "unos" and "otros" with a comma, as the Greek does, so Literal needs no supplied "[dicen]" where the English supplies "[say]".

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "you" (R), with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in Mark 8:28: Readable supplies "you", and the disciples call Jesus "Thầy", a noun of address that takes no setting span.

decisions.choice: "Giê-rê-mi"; "Giăng Báp-tít"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms of the names.

decisions.choice: "세례자 요한"; "예레미야"; "예언자"
decisions.reason: The forms settled for the Korean Matthew and Mark 8:28. Readable says "주님을" for the "you" the English supplies, as the disciples address Jesus in the Korean Matthew.

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι;

records.literal_gloss: He says to them, You but whom me do you say to be?

en.L: He says to them, "But you, who do you say that I am?"
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "And you, who do you say that I am?"
en.R: Then Jesus asked them, "What about you? Who do you say I am?"

es.B: Entonces les preguntó: «Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, ¿quién {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} que soy yo?».
es.R: Entonces Jesús les preguntó: «¿Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}? ¿Quién {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} que soy yo?».

fr.L: Il leur dit : « Mais vous, qui dites-vous que je suis ? »
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur demanda : « Et vous, qui dites-vous que je suis ? »
fr.R: Alors Jésus leur a demandé : « Et vous ? Qui dites-vous que je suis ? »

sw.B: Kisha akawauliza, "Na ninyi je, mnasema {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni nani?"
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawauliza, "Na ninyi je? Mnasema {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni nani?"

vi.L: Ngài nói với họ: "Còn các con, các con nói {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là ai?"
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi họ: "Còn các con, các con nói {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là ai?"
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu hỏi họ: "Còn các con thì sao? Các con nói {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là ai?"

ko.L: 그분이 그들에게 말씀하신다. "그러면 너희는 나를 누구라고 말하느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 물으셨다. "그러면 너희는 나를 누구라고 하느냐?"
ko.R: 그러자 예수께서 그들에게 물으셨다. "그러면 너희는 어떠냐? 너희는 나를 누구라고 하느냐?"

am.L: እርሱም ይላቸዋል፦ «እናንተ ግን እኔ ማን እንደ ሆንኩ ትላላችሁ?»
am.B: ከዚያም እንዲህ ሲል ጠየቃቸው፦ «እናንተስ እኔ ማን እንደ ሆንኩ ትላላችሁ?»
am.R: ከዚያም ኢየሱስ እንዲህ ብሎ ጠየቃቸው፦ «እናንተስ? እናንተ እኔን ማን ትሉኛላችሁ?»

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, the disciples set against the crowds
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands first for emphasis: whatever others say, what do you say?

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}
decisions.reason: Every plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes forms (Latin America, the default) or vosotros forms (Spain). English has no such choice. The same throughout the passage. The pronoun is kept because it is emphatic in the Greek (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}
decisions.reason: The English marks no span on "I". Swahili needs the free pronoun "mimi" here, and when Jesus speaks of himself a free pronoun takes the setting, as in John.

decisions.choice: "nói" with no "đã" (L) for the present "says"
decisions.reason: Matthew tells this in the present tense; Literal keeps it by leaving out the past marker.

decisions.choice: Present "말씀하신다" (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Matthew's present tense of narration.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος εἶπεν· Σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος.

records.literal_gloss: Answering then Simon Peter said, You are the Christ the Son of the God the living.

en.L: And Simon Peter answered and said, "You are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of the living God."
en.B: Simon Peter answered, "You are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of the living God."
en.R: Simon Peter answered, "You are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}. You are the Son of the God who lives."

es.L: Y respondiendo Simón Pedro, dijo: «Tú eres el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Hijo del Dios vivo».
es.B: Simón Pedro le respondió: «Tú eres el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Hijo del Dios vivo».
es.R: Simón Pedro contestó: «Tú eres el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}. Eres el Hijo del Dios que vive».

fr.L: Et Simon Pierre répondit et dit : « Tu es le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, le Fils du Dieu vivant. »
fr.B: Simon Pierre répondit : « Tu es le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, le Fils du Dieu vivant. »
fr.R: Simon Pierre a répondu : « Tu es le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Tu es le Fils du Dieu qui est vivant. »

sw.L: Na Simoni Petro akajibu, akasema, "Wewe ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mwana wa Mungu aliye hai."
sw.B: Simoni Petro alijibu, "Wewe ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mwana wa Mungu aliye hai."
sw.R: Simoni Petro alijibu, "Wewe ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Wewe ni Mwana wa Mungu anayeishi."

vi.L: Si-môn Phi-e-rơ đáp lời và thưa: "Thầy là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, Con của Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống."
vi.B: Si-môn Phi-e-rơ thưa: "Thầy là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, Con của Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống."
vi.R: Si-môn Phi-e-rơ trả lời: "Thầy là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}. Thầy là Con của Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng đang sống."

ko.L: 시몬 베드로가 대답하여 말했다. "주님은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이시며, 살아 계신 하나님의 아들이십니다."
ko.B: 시몬 베드로가 대답했다. "주님은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이시며, 살아 계신 하나님의 아들이십니다."
ko.R: 시몬 베드로가 대답했다. "주님은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이십니다. 살아 계신 하나님의 아들이십니다!"

am.L: ስምዖን ጴጥሮስም መልሶ አለ፦ «አንተ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}}፣ የሕያው እግዚአብሔር ልጅ ነህ።»
am.B: ስምዖን ጴጥሮስም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «አንተ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}}፣ የሕያው እግዚአብሔር ልጅ ነህ።»
am.R: ስምዖን ጴጥሮስም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «አንተ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} ነህ። አንተ የሕያው እግዚአብሔር ልጅ ነህ።»

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king God promised
decisions.reason: The word has the article: Peter names Jesus as the one Israel was waiting for. Herod's advisers spoke of the Christ in the same way (2:4).

decisions.choice: the Son of the living God: the Messiah as God's Son
alternatives: a second, separate title of lesser weight
decisions.reason: God promised to be father to David's royal son (2 Samuel 7:14; Psalm 2:7). Matthew has already shown God calling Jesus his Son (3:17), and the disciples saying so in the boat (14:33).

decisions.choice: the living God: the true God, who lives and acts
decisions.reason: The phrase sets God apart from idols that have no life (Jeremiah 10:10; Psalm 42:3).

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Where the Greek has the article, the title is written "the Christ" or "the Messiah".

decisions.choice: the God who lives
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "living" means.

decisions.choice: el Dios vivo
decisions.reason: "Vivo" is the ordinary Spanish adjective for one who lives; "viviente" is a more formal word for the same thing. Readable says "el Dios que vive", as the English Readable does (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "you" in Peter's confession
decisions.reason: As in Mark 8:29: the disciples call Jesus "Thầy"; Peter names who he is with the titles themselves. "Chúa" would read the church's later address into the scene.

decisions.choice: "Đức Chúa Trời hằng sống" (L, B); "Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng đang sống" (R)
decisions.reason: "Hằng sống" (ever-living) is the familiar phrase for the true God who lives and acts (meaning decision); Readable says it in plain words.

decisions.choice: "주님은" for "you", with the honorific "이십니다"; {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}
decisions.reason: Korean does not say "you" to the one being confessed; in the Korean Matthew the disciples address Jesus as "주님" (8:25, 14:28-33), so "주님" stands for the pronoun and is not bracketed. The christos span is the style guide's (section 7).

decisions.choice: "살아 계신 하나님" at every level
decisions.reason: The living God is the true God who lives and acts (meaning decision); the honorific "계신" is the natural Korean for God.

decisions.choice: "አንተ" (familiar you) from Peter to Jesus
decisions.reason: As the Amharic style guide sets for the whole Bible, people speak to Jesus with "አንተ", the familiar address Scripture uses also for God; respect is carried by what is said ("ጌታ ሆይ", the confession itself), not by the pronoun.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακάριος εἶ, Σίμων Βαριωνᾶ, ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα οὐκ ἀπεκάλυψέν σοι ἀλλ’ ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: Answering then Jesus said to him, Blessed are you, Simon Barjona, for flesh and blood not revealed to you but the Father of me who in the heavens;

en.L: And Jesus answered and said to him, "Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, for flesh and blood did not reveal [this] to you, but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who [is] in the heavens.
en.B: Jesus said to him in reply, "You are blessed, Simon son of Jonah! No human being showed you this; it was {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven.
en.R: Jesus answered, "Simon son of Jonah, God has blessed you! No person showed you this. My Father in heaven showed it to you.

es.L: Y respondiendo Jesús, le dijo: «Dichoso tú, Simón Bar Jonás, pues carne y sangre no te [lo] revelaron, sino {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre, el [que está] en los cielos.
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «¡Dichoso tú, Simón, hijo de Jonás! No fue ningún ser humano quien te mostró esto, sino {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre que está en el cielo.
es.R: Jesús le respondió: «Simón, hijo de Jonás, ¡Dios te ha bendecido! Ninguna persona te mostró esto. Mi Padre que está en el cielo te lo mostró.

fr.L: Et Jésus répondit et lui dit : « Heureux es-tu, Simon Bar-Jona, car ce ne sont pas la chair et le sang qui te [l’]ont révélé, mais {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui [est] dans les cieux.
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Tu es heureux, Simon, fils de Jonas ! Ce n’est pas un être humain qui t’a fait connaître cela, c’est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui est au ciel.
fr.R: Jésus lui a répondu : « Simon, fils de Jonas, Dieu t’a béni ! Ce n’est pas une personne qui t’a fait connaître cela. Mon Père qui est au ciel te l’a montré.

sw.L: Na Yesu akajibu, akamwambia, "Heri wewe, Simoni Bar-Yona, kwa sababu mwili na damu havikukufunulia [jambo hili], ila Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni.
sw.B: Yesu alimjibu, "Heri wewe, Simoni mwana wa Yona! Hakuna binadamu aliyekuonyesha jambo hili; ni Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni.
sw.R: Yesu alimjibu, "Simoni mwana wa Yona, Mungu amekubariki! Hakuna mtu aliyekuonyesha jambo hili. Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni ndiye aliyekuonyesha.

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu đáp lời và nói với ông: "Phước cho con, Si-môn Ba-giô-na, vì không phải thịt và máu đã bày tỏ [điều này] cho con, nhưng là Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, Đấng ở trên các tầng trời.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Phước cho con, Si-môn con Giô-na! Không phải loài người đã bày tỏ điều này cho con, nhưng chính Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trên trời.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Si-môn con Giô-na, Đức Chúa Trời đã ban phước cho con! Không phải người nào đã cho con biết điều này. Chính Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trên trời đã cho con biết.

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 대답하여 그에게 말씀하셨다. "시몬 바요나야, 너는 복이 있다. 혈과 육이 [이것을] 너에게 드러낸 것이 아니라, 하늘들에 계신 내 아버지께서 [드러내셨기] 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "요나의 아들 시몬아, 너는 복이 있다! 사람이 이것을 너에게 알려 준 것이 아니라, 하늘에 계신 내 아버지께서 알려 주셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "요나의 아들 시몬아, 하나님께서 너에게 복을 주셨다! 이것을 너에게 알려 준 것은 사람이 아니다. 하늘에 계신 내 아버지께서 알려 주셨다.

am.L: ኢየሱስም መልሶ እንዲህ አለው፦ «ስምዖን በርዮና ሆይ፣ የተባረክ ነህ፤ ሥጋና ደም [ይህን] አልገለጠልህምና፣ በሰማያት ያለው አባቴ እንጂ።
am.B: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ ሲል መለሰለት፦ «የዮና ልጅ ስምዖን፣ የተባረክ ነህ! ይህን የገለጠልህ ሰው አይደለም፤ በሰማይ ያለው አባቴ ነው።
am.R: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰለት፦ «የዮና ልጅ ስምዖን ሆይ፣ እግዚአብሔር ባርኮሃል! ይህን ያሳየህ ሰው አይደለም። ይህን ያሳየህ በሰማይ ያለው አባቴ ነው።

decisions.choice: Bar-Jonah: son of Jonah, an Aramaic way of naming a man by his father
decisions.reason: "Bar" means "son" in Aramaic. John 1:42 and 21:15 call Simon's father John; the two forms may be versions of one name, or Jonah may be another name he had.

decisions.choice: flesh and blood: a human being, as opposed to God
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of humans in their weakness (1 Corinthians 15:50; Galatians 1:16). Peter did not reach this by human insight.

decisions.choice: revealed: made known what was hidden
decisions.reason: As in 11:25-27, the Father shows who the Son is to those he chooses.

decisions.choice: blessed: favored by God, as in 5:3-11
decisions.reason: Peter is in the happy state of one God has favored.

decisions.choice: Bar-Jonah (L); son of Jonah (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic form with a hyphen; Balanced and Readable translate it.

decisions.choice: God has blessed you
decisions.reason: Readable says who gives the blessing.

decisions.choice: Dichoso
decisions.reason: "Dichoso" says plainly that God has favored Peter (meaning decision m4), as in John 20:29; "bienaventurado" is the older church word. Readable says "Dios te ha bendecido", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Heureux (L, B), as in the Beatitudes; Bar-Jona (L), fils de Jonas (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is the one of 5:3-11 (m4), which French renders "Heureux"; Readable follows the English "God has blessed you". "Bar-Jona" is the usual French spelling of the Aramaic name; Jonah is "Jonas" in French.

decisions.choice: havikukufunulia [jambo hili]
decisions.reason: "Mwili na damu" (flesh and blood, meaning decision m2) take the agreement "vi-" that Swahili uses for two things joined. The verb needs an object, which the Greek leaves out, so Literal supplies "[jambo hili]", as the English supplies "[this]".

decisions.choice: "Ba-giô-na" (L); "con Giô-na" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic form of the name, transliterated; Balanced and Readable say what it means, son of Jonah (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "thịt và máu" (L); "loài người" (B); "người nào" (R); "Phước cho con"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom, which means a human being as opposed to God (meaning decision). "Phước cho" as in the Beatitudes (5:3); Jesus calls Peter "con", as he speaks to his disciples.

decisions.choice: "바요나" (L); "요나의 아들" (B, R); "복이 있다" (L, B); "혈과 육" (L), "사람" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Bar-Jonah means son of Jonah (meaning decision); Literal keeps the Aramaic name in its Protestant form, the other levels say what it means. "복이 있다" is the Korean Matthew's word from the Beatitudes; "flesh and blood" means a human being (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "하늘들에 계신" (L); "하늘에 계신" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Matthew 5:16 and 12:50: Literal keeps the Greek plural "heavens".

decisions.choice: "የተባረክ ነህ" (you are blessed)
decisions.reason: "ብፁዕ" is Ge'ez and sounds liturgical; "ደስተኛ" says only how Simon feels. "የተባረክ" says that God has favoured him, as in 5:3-11, and Readable makes God the subject, as the English Readable does.

source.text: κἀγὼ δέ σοι λέγω ὅτι σὺ εἶ Πέτρος, καὶ ἐπὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πέτρᾳ οἰκοδομήσω μου τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, καὶ πύλαι ᾅδου οὐ κατισχύσουσιν αὐτῆς·

records.literal_gloss: I also now to you say that you are Peter, and on this the rock I will build of me the church, and gates of Hades not will prevail against it;

en.L: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} church, and [the] gates of Hades will not overpower it.
en.B: And I tell you: you are Peter, and on this rock I will build {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} church. The gates of the realm of the dead will not overpower it.
en.R: And I tell you, you are Peter. (The name Peter means "rock.") On this rock I will build {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} church. Even the gates of the place of the dead will not be strong enough to defeat it.

es.L: Y también yo te digo que tú eres Pedro, y sobre esta roca construiré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} iglesia, y [las] puertas del Hades no la vencerán.
es.B: Y yo te digo: tú eres Pedro, y sobre esta roca construiré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} iglesia. Las puertas del Hades no podrán vencerla.
es.R: Y yo te digo que tú eres Pedro. (El nombre Pedro quiere decir “roca”). Sobre esta roca construiré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} iglesia. Ni siquiera las puertas del lugar de los muertos tendrán fuerza para vencerla.

fr.L: Et moi aussi, je te dis que tu es Pierre, et sur cette pierre je bâtirai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Église, et [les] portes de l’Hadès ne l’emporteront pas sur elle.
fr.B: Et moi, je te le dis : tu es Pierre, et sur cette pierre je bâtirai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Église. Les portes du séjour des morts ne pourront pas la vaincre.
fr.R: Et moi, je te le dis : tu es Pierre. Ton nom veut dire “pierre”. Sur cette pierre, je vais construire {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Église. Même les portes du séjour des morts ne seront pas assez fortes pour la vaincre.

sw.L: Nami pia nakuambia kwamba wewe ni Petro, na juu ya mwamba huu nitajenga kanisa {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, na malango ya Kuzimu hayatalizidi nguvu.
sw.B: Nami nakuambia: wewe ni Petro, na juu ya mwamba huu nitalijenga kanisa {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. Malango ya Kuzimu hayataweza kulishinda.
sw.R: Nami nakuambia, wewe ni Petro. (Jina Petro maana yake ni 'mwamba.') Juu ya mwamba huu nitajenga kanisa {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. Hata malango ya Kuzimu, mahali pa wafu, hayatakuwa na nguvu za kulishinda.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng nói với con rằng con là Phi-e-rơ, và trên tảng đá này {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xây Hội Thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và các cửa Ha-đét sẽ không thắng được Hội Thánh ấy.
vi.B: Ta cũng nói với con: con là Phi-e-rơ, và trên tảng đá này {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xây Hội Thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Các cửa âm phủ sẽ không thắng nổi Hội Thánh ấy.
vi.R: Ta cũng nói với con: con là Phi-e-rơ. (Tên Phi-e-rơ có nghĩa là 'đá'.) Trên tảng đá này {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xây Hội Thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ngay cả các cửa của nơi người chết cũng không đủ sức thắng được Hội Thánh ấy.

ko.L: 그리고 나도 너에게 말한다. 너는 베드로이다. 그리고 이 바위 위에 내가 내 교회를 세울 것이다. 하데스의 문들이 그것을 이기지 못할 것이다.
ko.B: 나도 너에게 말한다. 너는 베드로이다. 내가 이 바위 위에 내 교회를 세울 것이다. 죽은 사람들의 세계의 문들도 교회를 이기지 못할 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 너에게 말한다. 너는 베드로이다. (베드로라는 이름은 '바위'라는 뜻이다.) 내가 이 바위 위에 내 교회를 세울 것이다. 죽은 사람들이 가는 곳의 문들도 교회를 이기지 못할 것이다.

am.L: እኔም ደግሞ አንተ ጴጥሮስ እንደ ሆንህ እልሃለሁ፤ በዚህችም ዓለት ላይ ቤተ ክርስቲያኔን እሠራለሁ፤ የሲኦል ደጆችም አያሸንፏትም።
am.B: እኔም እልሃለሁ፤ አንተ ጴጥሮስ ነህ፤ በዚህም ዓለት ላይ ቤተ ክርስቲያኔን እሠራለሁ። የሲኦል ደጆች አያሸንፏትም።
am.R: እኔም እልሃለሁ፤ አንተ ጴጥሮስ ነህ። (ጴጥሮስ ማለት “ዓለት” ማለት ነው።) በዚህ ዓለት ላይ ቤተ ክርስቲያኔን እሠራለሁ። የሙታን መኖሪያ ደጆች እንኳ ሊያሸንፏት አይችሉም።

decisions.choice: Peter and rock: a play on words
decisions.reason: The name Peter means a stone or rock, and the word for "rock" that follows comes from the same root. In Aramaic, which Jesus spoke, both would be the same word, Kepha, the name Cephas (John 1:42). Jesus gave Simon this name (10:2).

decisions.choice: this rock: Peter himself, as the apostle who has confessed Jesus
alternatives: Peter's confession of who Jesus is
the truth revealed by the Father
decisions.reason: The play on Peter's name points most naturally to Peter, who leads the apostles in the early church (Acts 2-5; Ephesians 2:20 speaks of apostles as the foundation). Others take the rock to be the faith Peter has just confessed, or Christ himself (1 Corinthians 3:11; 1 Peter 2:4-8). Christian traditions have long differed here.

decisions.choice: church: the community of Jesus's people
decisions.reason: This is the first time the word appears in the Gospels. It meant an assembly, and the Greek Old Testament uses it for the assembly of Israel gathered before God (Deuteronomy 4:10). Jesus speaks of the people he will gather as his own.

decisions.choice: the gates of Hades will not overpower it: the power of death will not overcome the church
alternatives: the church will break through the gates of Hades
evil powers will not defeat it
decisions.reason: Gates stand for a city's strength. The Old Testament speaks of "the gates of death" and "the gates of Sheol" (Isaiah 38:10; Psalm 9:14). Death will not hold or destroy the people Jesus builds. Hades is the realm of the dead, as in 11:23.

decisions.choice: Hades (L); the realm of the dead (B); the place of the dead (R)
decisions.reason: As in 11:23. "Hell" would confuse Hades with Gehenna.

decisions.choice: (The name Peter means "rock.")
decisions.reason: Readable explains the play on words, which cannot be heard in translation. It does not say what the rock is.

decisions.choice: church
decisions.reason: "Church" is the familiar word for the community Jesus gathers; the meaning decision says it is people, not a building.

decisions.choice: will not be strong enough to defeat
decisions.reason: Readable puts the verb in plain words.

decisions.choice: Pedro ... roca; Readable explains «Pedro quiere decir “roca”»
decisions.reason: The play on words (meaning decision m1) cannot be kept in Spanish, where the name Pedro is not the word for rock. "Roca" is the large mass of rock a building stands on; "piedra" would sound like the name but means a single stone. Readable explains the name, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: el Hades (L, B); el lugar de los muertos (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish: "Hades" is a known Spanish word for the realm of the dead, so Balanced keeps it where the English Balanced explains it; Readable says "el lugar de los muertos", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Pierre … cette pierre, at every level
decisions.reason: French can keep the play on words (m1) that English cannot: the name "Pierre" and the noun "pierre" are the same word. "Roc" or "rocher" would be closer to the size of the Greek word for rock but would lose the pun. Readable still says in one short sentence that the name means "pierre", as the English Readable explains it, and like the English does not say what the rock is.

decisions.choice: mon Église (for the whole book); l’Hadès (L), le séjour des morts (B, R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's terms: "l’Église" with a capital for the whole community of Jesus's people (m3), not one congregation or a building; Hades as in Luke 10:15. "L’enfer" would confuse Hades with Gehenna, as the English decision says.

decisions.choice: Petro ... mwamba; Readable explains the name
decisions.reason: The play on words (meaning decision m1) cannot be kept in Swahili, where the name Petro is not the word for rock. "Mwamba" is solid rock a building can stand on; "jiwe" is a single stone. Readable explains the name, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Kuzimu at every level; Readable adds "mahali pa wafu"
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili: "Kuzimu" is the world below, the place of the dead, as in Romans 10:7, so it serves where the English Balanced explains "Hades". Readable adds the explanation, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Hội Thánh" at every level
decisions.reason: The Protestant word for the community of Jesus's people (meaning decision), as in the Vietnamese Colossians; capitalised as there.

decisions.choice: "Ha-đét" (L); "âm phủ" (B); "nơi người chết" (R)
decisions.reason: The forms of Matthew 11:23: Hades is the place of the dead, not of punishment ("địa ngục" is Gehenna).

decisions.choice: "(Tên Phi-e-rơ có nghĩa là 'đá'.)" (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot show the play on "Peter" and "rock" (meaning decision), so Readable explains it, as the English Readable does; "tảng đá" at every level keeps the second half of the pun.

decisions.choice: "베드로" ... "바위"; Readable explains the name
decisions.reason: Korean cannot keep the play on "Petros" and "petra" (meaning decision), since "베드로" is only a name to Korean readers; Readable adds what the name means, as the English Readable does. "바위" is the everyday word; "반석" is the older church word.

decisions.choice: "교회" at every level; "하데스" (L), "죽은 사람들의 세계" (B), "죽은 사람들이 가는 곳" (R)
decisions.reason: "교회" is the word of the Korean letters (Colossians 1:18) and says the community of Jesus's people (meaning decision). Hades is worded as in the Korean Matthew 11:23 and Luke 10:15 at every level; Readable keeps the gates, as the English Readable does, since the picture of a city's strength is plain (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "ዓለት" (rock, bedrock) for the rock
decisions.reason: The Greek word is bedrock, the foundation a house is built on, not a loose stone. Amharic cannot reproduce the play between the names "ጴጥሮስ" and the rock, so Literal and Balanced rely on the meaning decision, and Readable explains it in brackets as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ሲኦል" (L, B); "የሙታን መኖሪያ" (the dwelling of the dead, R)
decisions.reason: "ሲኦል" is the Amharic word for the realm of the dead, kept apart from "ገሃነም", the place of punishment (Gehenna). Readable says what it is in plain words.

decisions.choice: the keys: authority to open and shut, like a royal steward's
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 22:22 God gives the steward of David's house the key to open and shut. Peter is given authority in the kingdom; Jesus condemns the scribes for shutting it (23:13).

decisions.choice: bind and loose: forbid and permit, and so declare what God requires or forgives
alternatives: condemn and set free from sin only
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers used these words for ruling what is forbidden and what is allowed. In 18:18 the same words are given to all the disciples about a sinning member of the church; compare John 20:23 on forgiving sins.

decisions.choice: will be bound: heaven confirms what is done on earth
alternatives: will already have been bound: earth carries out what heaven has decided
decisions.reason: The verb form joins "will be" with a perfect participle. It may simply mean "will be bound", or stress that heaven has decided first.

decisions.choice: forbid; allow
decisions.reason: Readable uses the sense of the Jewish teachers' terms, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: el reino de los cielos
decisions.reason: Matthew's name for God's kingdom, said the same way at every level throughout the book. The Spanish plural "los cielos" is natural in this phrase, as the Greek plural is; elsewhere Balanced and Readable say "el cielo".

decisions.choice: quedará atado; quedará desatado
decisions.reason: The Greek says that what is bound "will be, having been bound" (meaning decision m3). "Quedará atado" keeps the sense of a state that heaven holds to, without saying which comes first.

decisions.choice: le royaume des cieux at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide's term, kept at Readable as the English keeps "kingdom of heaven".

decisions.choice: ufalme wa mbinguni
decisions.reason: Matthew's name for God's kingdom, said the same way at every level throughout the book. "Mbinguni" (in heaven) is the natural Swahili form of the phrase and covers the Greek plural "heavens".

decisions.choice: "buộc" and "mở" (L, B); "cấm" and "cho phép" (R)
decisions.reason: Bind and loose mean forbid and permit (meaning decision); Literal and Balanced keep the picture in plain words, Readable gives the sense, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "trên các tầng trời" (L); "trên trời" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled Matthew forms for "in the heavens"; "vương quốc thiên đàng" at every level.

decisions.choice: "천국" at every level
decisions.reason: "Kingdom of the heavens" is "천국" at every level, as settled for the Korean Matthew.

decisions.choice: "매다", "풀다" (L, B); "금하다", "허락하다" (R); "매여 있을 것이다" (L)
decisions.reason: Bind and loose mean forbid and permit (meaning decision, with footnote); Literal and Balanced keep the picture, Readable says what it means. Literal keeps the Greek perfect, a state already settled in heaven (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "መንግሥተ ሰማያት" (L, B); "የሰማይ መንግሥት" (R)
decisions.reason: "መንግሥተ ሰማያት" is the living church name for the kingdom of heaven and keeps the Greek plural "heavens"; Readable uses the plain Amharic phrase every reader understands. Used so for the rest of these chapters.

decisions.choice: tell no one: not yet, before he has taught what kind of Messiah he is
decisions.reason: Many expected a Messiah who would drive out Rome. From 16:21 Jesus teaches that the Messiah must suffer, and after his resurrection the disciples are sent to tell all nations (28:19).

decisions.choice: ordered ... the Christ, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: warned (or rebuked), the reading of some manuscripts
Jesus the Christ, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have a stronger verb for the order, and many add the name "Jesus" before "the Christ". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus

decisions.choice: discípulos at every level
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "followers", Spanish keeps "discípulos", a common word every reader knows, as in John. The same through the passage.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi at every level
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "followers", Swahili keeps "wanafunzi", the everyday word for a teacher's disciples, as in John. The same through the passage.

records.literal_gloss: From then began Jesus to show to the disciples of him that it is necessary for him to Jerusalem to go away and many things to suffer from the elders and chief priests and scribes and to be killed and on the third day to be raised.

en.L: From then Jesus began to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must go away to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and on the third day be raised.
en.B: From then on Jesus began to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples plainly that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must go to Jerusalem. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would suffer much from the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would be killed, and on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would be raised.
en.R: From that time Jesus began to explain to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers what must happen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He had to go to Jerusalem. There the elders, the leading priests, and the teachers of the law would make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} suffer many things. He would be killed. Then on the third day God would raise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from death.

es.L: Desde entonces comenzó Jesús a mostrar a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} debía irse a Jerusalén y padecer mucho de parte de los ancianos y principales sacerdotes y escribas, y ser muerto, y al tercer día ser resucitado.
es.B: Desde entonces Jesús comenzó a mostrar claramente a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos que tenía que ir a Jerusalén. Allí sufriría mucho a manos de los ancianos, los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas; {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} matarían, y al tercer día sería resucitado.
es.R: Desde ese momento, Jesús comenzó a explicar a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tenía que pasar. Tenía que ir a Jerusalén. Allí los ancianos, los jefes de los sacerdotes y los maestros de la ley {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} harían sufrir mucho. Lo matarían. Luego, al tercer día, Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} resucitaría de la muerte.

fr.L: Dès lors, Jésus commença à montrer à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples qu’il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} fallait s’en aller à Jérusalem, et souffrir beaucoup de la part des anciens, des chefs des prêtres et des scribes, et être mis à mort, et le troisième jour être ressuscité.
fr.B: À partir de ce moment, Jésus commença à montrer clairement à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} devait aller à Jérusalem. Là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} souffrirait beaucoup de la part des anciens, des chefs des prêtres et des scribes ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} serait mis à mort, et le troisième jour {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} serait ressuscité.
fr.R: À partir de ce moment-là, Jésus a commencé à expliquer à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ce qui devait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} arriver. Il devait aller à Jérusalem. Là, les responsables du peuple, les chefs des prêtres et les spécialistes de la Loi allaient {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire beaucoup souffrir. On allait {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tuer. Puis, le troisième jour, Dieu allait {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ramener à la vie.

sw.L: Kuanzia hapo Yesu alianza kuwaonyesha wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwamba ni lazima aende Yerusalemu, na kuteswa mengi na wazee na wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi, na kuuawa, na siku ya tatu kufufuliwa.
sw.B: Kuanzia wakati huo Yesu alianza kuwaeleza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waziwazi kwamba ilimlazimu kwenda Yerusalemu. Huko angeteswa sana na wazee, wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi; angeuawa, na siku ya tatu angefufuliwa.
sw.R: Tangu wakati huo, Yesu alianza kuwaeleza wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mambo ambayo yangempata. Ilimbidi aende Yerusalemu. Huko wazee, wakuu wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria wangemtesa sana. Angeuawa. Kisha siku ya tatu Mungu angemfufua kutoka kwa wafu.

vi.L: Từ lúc đó, Đức Giê-xu bắt đầu tỏ cho các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phải đi đến Giê-ru-sa-lem, chịu nhiều đau khổ bởi các trưởng lão, các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo, và bị giết, và đến ngày thứ ba được sống lại.
vi.B: Từ đó, Đức Giê-xu bắt đầu tỏ rõ cho các môn đồ biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phải đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Tại đó {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ chịu nhiều đau khổ bởi các trưởng lão, các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ bị giết, và đến ngày thứ ba sẽ được sống lại.
vi.R: Từ lúc ấy, Đức Giê-xu bắt đầu giải thích cho các môn đồ những gì phải xảy đến cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài phải đi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Tại đó, các nhà lãnh đạo của dân, các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy dạy luật sẽ làm cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chịu nhiều đau khổ. Ngài sẽ bị giết. Rồi đến ngày thứ ba, Đức Chúa Trời sẽ làm cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sống lại.

ko.L: 그때부터 예수께서 자기 제자들에게, 자기가 예루살렘으로 가서 장로들과 대제사장들과 율법학자들에게 많은 고난을 받고, 죽임을 당하고, 셋째 날에 살아나셔야 한다는 것을 보여 주기 시작하셨다.
ko.B: 그때부터 예수께서는 제자들에게, 자기가 반드시 예루살렘에 가서 장로들과 대제사장들과 율법학자들에게 많은 고난을 받으시고, 죽임을 당하시고, 셋째 날에 다시 살아나셔야 한다는 것을 분명히 알려 주기 시작하셨다.
ko.R: 그때부터 예수께서는 앞으로 자기에게 일어날 일을 제자들에게 설명해 주기 시작하셨다. 예수께서는 예루살렘으로 가셔야 했다. 거기서 백성의 지도자들과 대제사장들과 율법 선생들이 예수께 많은 고난을 줄 것이다. 예수께서는 죽임을 당하실 것이다. 그러나 셋째 날에 하나님께서 예수를 다시 살리실 것이다.

am.L: ከዚያን ጊዜ ጀምሮ ኢየሱስ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ሄዶ ከሽማግሌዎችና ከካህናት አለቆች ከጸሐፍትም ብዙ መከራ ሊቀበል፣ ሊገደልም፣ በሦስተኛውም ቀን ሊነሣ እንደሚገባው ለደቀ መዛሙርቱ ማሳየት ጀመረ።
am.B: ከዚያን ጊዜ ጀምሮ ኢየሱስ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም መሄድ እንዳለበት ለደቀ መዛሙርቱ በግልጽ ማሳየት ጀመረ። በዚያም ከሽማግሌዎች፣ ከካህናት አለቆችና ከሕግ መምህራን ብዙ መከራ ይቀበላል፤ ይገደላል፤ በሦስተኛውም ቀን ይነሣል።
am.R: ከዚያን ጊዜ ጀምሮ ኢየሱስ በእርሱ ላይ የሚደርሰውን ነገር ለደቀ መዛሙርቱ ማስረዳት ጀመረ። ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም መሄድ ነበረበት። በዚያም ሽማግሌዎች፣ የካህናት አለቆችና የሕግ መምህራን ብዙ መከራ ያደርሱበታል። ይገደላል። በሦስተኛው ቀን ግን እግዚአብሔር ከሞት ያስነሣዋል።

decisions.choice: from then Jesus began: the start of a new stage of the story
decisions.reason: Matthew used the same words in 4:17 when Jesus began to preach. Now he begins to speak of his death.

decisions.choice: must: it is God's will and plan
decisions.reason: The suffering is what God has purposed and Scripture foretold (26:54).

decisions.choice: be raised: raised by God
decisions.reason: The passive verb leaves God unnamed as the one who raises Jesus, as often in the New Testament (Acts 2:24).

decisions.choice: the elders, chief priests and scribes: the groups that made up the Jewish council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Together they formed the ruling council; they condemn Jesus in 26:57-66.

decisions.choice: the wording of 4:17 at each level
decisions.reason: The same opening words are given the same English, so readers can see the parallel.

decisions.choice: God would raise him from death
decisions.reason: Readable names God, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: los escribas (L, B); los maestros de la ley (R)
alternatives: los maestros de la ley (every level)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish: "escribas" is the familiar name for these experts in the Law of Moses; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable says "teachers of the law".

decisions.choice: les anciens, les chefs des prêtres, les scribes (L, B); les responsables du peuple, les chefs des prêtres, les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's terms for the three groups of the council (m4), as in Mark 8:31 and Luke 9:22. Readable says who the elders were, as Mark's and Luke's French do, and keeps "les chefs des prêtres", which is already plain.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili: "waandishi" is the familiar name for these experts in the Law of Moses; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable says "teachers of the law".

decisions.choice: "Từ lúc đó" (L), "Từ đó" (B), "Từ lúc ấy" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of 4:17 at each level, since Matthew opens a new stage of the story with the same phrase (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "các trưởng lão" (L, B), "các nhà lãnh đạo của dân" (R); "các thầy tế lễ cả"; "các thầy thông giáo" (L, B), "các thầy dạy luật" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled terms, as in Mark 8:31. Readable names God as the one who raises him (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "그때부터", as in the Korean Matthew 4:17; "장로들" (L, B), "백성의 지도자들" (R); "대제사장들"; "율법학자들" (L, B), "율법 선생들" (R)
decisions.reason: Matthew repeats the opening of 4:17, so the Korean does too. The three groups of the council (meaning decision) are worded as in the Korean Mark 8:31 and Matthew 8:19.

decisions.choice: "살아나셔야" (L, B); "하나님께서 예수를 다시 살리실 것이다" (R)
decisions.reason: The passive means raised by God (meaning decision); a Korean passive of "일으키다" would be stilted, so Literal and Balanced use "살아나다" as the Korean Mark 8:31 does, and Readable names God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ጸሐፍት" (L); "የሕግ መምህራን" (teachers of the Law, B, R)
decisions.reason: "ጸሐፍት" is the traditional word, but to most readers it means clerks or copyists; the scribes were teachers and interpreters of the Law, so Balanced and Readable say so. Used so for the rest of these chapters.

source.text: καὶ προσλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ὁ Πέτρος ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ λέγων· Ἵλεώς σοι, κύριε· οὐ μὴ ἔσται σοι τοῦτο.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken aside him Peter began to rebuke him saying, Merciful to you, Lord; never will be to you this.

en.L: And Peter took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} aside and began to rebuke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "[God be] merciful to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord! This will never happen to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: Peter drew {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} aside and began to object. "God forbid it, Lord!" he said. "Nothing like this will ever happen to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"
en.R: Peter took Jesus aside and began to tell {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was wrong. "No, Lord!" he said. "May God keep this from ever happening to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

es.L: Y Pedro, tomándolo aparte, comenzó a reprenderlo, diciendo: «¡[Dios tenga] compasión de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, Señor! Esto no {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} sucederá jamás».
es.B: Pedro {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevó aparte y comenzó a protestar: «¡Dios no lo quiera, Señor! ¡Eso nunca {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} va a pasar!».
es.R: Pedro llevó a Jesús aparte y empezó a decirle que estaba equivocado: «¡No, Señor! ¡Que Dios no permita que eso {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pase nunca!».

fr.L: Et Pierre, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} prenant à part, se mit à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} réprimander, disant : « [Que Dieu] {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} [soit] favorable, Seigneur ! Cela ne {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}arrivera jamais. »
fr.B: Pierre {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} prit à part et se mit à protester : « Dieu {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en garde, Seigneur ! dit-il. Rien de tel ne {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}arrivera jamais ! »
fr.R: Pierre a pris Jésus à part et s’est mis à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dire qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait tort. « Non, Seigneur ! a-t-il dit. Que Dieu ne permette jamais que cela {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}arrive ! »

sw.L: Na Petro akamchukua kando, akaanza kumkemea, akisema, "[Mungu] akuhurumie, Bwana! Jambo hili halitakupata kamwe."
sw.B: Petro alimchukua kando, akaanza kumpinga: "Mungu apishe mbali, Bwana! Jambo kama hili halitakupata kamwe!"
sw.R: Petro alimchukua Yesu kando, akaanza kumwambia kwamba amekosea. Akasema, "Hapana, Bwana! Mungu asiruhusu jambo hili likupate hata kidogo!"

vi.L: Và Phi-e-rơ kéo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} riêng ra và bắt đầu can gián {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nói rằng: "Lạy Chúa, [xin Đức Chúa Trời] thương xót Chúa! Điều ấy sẽ không bao giờ xảy đến cho Chúa đâu."
vi.B: Phi-e-rơ kéo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra một bên và bắt đầu can ngăn: "Lạy Chúa, xin Đức Chúa Trời đừng để như thế! Điều đó sẽ không bao giờ xảy đến cho Chúa!"
vi.R: Phi-e-rơ kéo Đức Giê-xu ra một bên và bắt đầu nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói sai. Ông nói: "Không được đâu, lạy Chúa! Xin Đức Chúa Trời đừng bao giờ để điều đó xảy đến cho Chúa!"

ko.L: 그러자 베드로가 그분을 따로 모시고 가서 그분을 꾸짖기 시작하며 말했다. "주님, [하나님께서] 주님께 자비를 [베푸시기를 빕니다]. 이런 일이 결코 주님께 일어나지 않을 것입니다."
ko.B: 그러자 베드로가 예수를 따로 모시고 가서 항의하기 시작했다. "주님, 절대로 안 됩니다! 이런 일이 주님께 일어나서는 결코 안 됩니다!"
ko.R: 그러자 베드로가 예수를 따로 모시고 갔다. 그리고 그렇게 말씀하시면 안 된다고 말리기 시작했다. "주님, 안 됩니다! 하나님께서 이런 일이 주님께 절대로 일어나지 않게 지켜 주시기를 빕니다!"

am.L: ጴጥሮስም ለብቻው ወስዶት እንዲህ እያለ ይገሥጸው ጀመር፦ «ጌታ ሆይ፣ [እግዚአብሔር] ይራራልህ፤ ይህ ከቶ አይደርስብህም።»
am.B: ጴጥሮስ ለብቻው ወስዶት ይቃወመው ጀመር። «ጌታ ሆይ፣ እግዚአብሔር ያርቀው!» አለ። «እንዲህ ያለ ነገር ከቶ አይደርስብህም!»
am.R: ጴጥሮስ ኢየሱስን ለብቻው ወሰደውና መሳሳቱን ይነግረው ጀመር። «አይሆንም፣ ጌታ ሆይ!» አለ። «እግዚአብሔር ይህን ከአንተ ያርቀው!»

decisions.choice: [God be] merciful to you: God forbid!
decisions.reason: The phrase was a common way of rejecting something strongly, wishing that God in mercy would spare someone from it.

decisions.choice: this will never happen: the strongest form of denial
decisions.reason: Two negatives together make the denial emphatic.

decisions.choice: rebuke: speak sharply against
decisions.reason: It is the same word used when Jesus rebukes the wind (8:26). Peter is correcting his teacher.

decisions.choice: tell him that he was wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what rebuking means here.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns: lo, ti, te; none on tomándolo, reprenderlo, decirle
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish joins an object pronoun to an infinitive or gerund ("reprenderlo"), and a capital inside the word would look like an error, so the setting covers only pronouns written as separate words, as in Mark 16. Spanish therefore has fewer spans than English here and in the rest of the passage.

decisions.choice: Mungu apishe mbali
decisions.reason: The Greek wishes God's mercy on Jesus and means "God forbid!" (meaning decision m1). "Mungu apishe mbali" (may God keep it far away) is the everyday Swahili way of saying that, and keeps God in the wish; Literal shows the Greek form with "[Mungu] akuhurumie".

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa" and "Chúa" for "you", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Matthew has Peter call Jesus "Lord"; the settled Matthew address for disciples, a noun that takes no setting span.

decisions.choice: "can gián" (L); "can ngăn" (B) for Peter's rebuke, against "quở trách" for Jesus in 16:23
decisions.reason: Here Jesus answers with a different verb (16:23 has no "rebuke"), and Vietnamese "quở trách" said by a disciple to his teacher would sound like a superior scolding; "can gián" is to remonstrate. Readable says what he did, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "꾸짖기" (L); "항의하기" (B); "그렇게 말씀하시면 안 된다고 말리기" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 8:32: Literal keeps the verb used of Jesus' rebukes; a disciple who "꾸짖는" his teacher is jarring in Korean, so Balanced and Readable say what Peter did.

decisions.choice: "[하나님께서] 주님께 자비를 [베푸시기를 빕니다]" (L); "절대로 안 됩니다!" (B); "하나님께서 ... 지켜 주시기를 빕니다" (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom means "God forbid!" (meaning decision). Literal shows its words, bracketing what Korean must supply; Balanced gives the force of the cry; Readable keeps the appeal to God, as the English Readable does. "그리 마옵소서" is archaic.

decisions.choice: "እግዚአብሔር ያርቀው" (may God keep it far away)
alternatives: "[እግዚአብሔር] ይራራልህ" (God be merciful to you), as Literal
decisions.reason: The Greek is a set phrase for warding off something terrible; the Amharic idiom "እግዚአብሔር ያርቀው" does the same work, while Literal keeps the Greek's own wording.

source.text: ὁ δὲ στραφεὶς εἶπεν τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου, Σατανᾶ· σκάνδαλον εἶ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

records.literal_gloss: He but having turned said to Peter, Get behind me, Satan; a stumbling block you are of me, for not you think the things of the God but the things of the men.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned and said to Peter, "Get behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Satan! You are a stumbling block to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for you do not think the things of God but the things of {{gender:people|men}}."
en.B: Jesus turned and said to Peter, "Get behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Satan! You are a stumbling block in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} way. Your mind is not on God's purposes but on human ones."
en.R: Jesus turned and said to Peter, "Get behind {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, Satan! You are trying to make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fall. You are not thinking the way God thinks. You are thinking the way people think."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, volviéndose, dijo a Pedro: «¡Ponte detrás de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, Satanás! Tropiezo eres para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque no tienes en mente las cosas de Dios, sino las de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}».
es.B: Jesús se volvió y dijo a Pedro: «¡Ponte detrás de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, Satanás! Eres un obstáculo en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} camino. No tienes en mente los propósitos de Dios, sino los humanos».
es.R: Jesús se volvió y le dijo a Pedro: «¡Ponte detrás de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, Satanás! Estás tratando de hacerme caer. No piensas como piensa Dios. Piensas como piensa la gente».

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, s’étant retourné, dit à Pierre : « Va derrière {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, Satan ! Tu es pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} une pierre d’achoppement, car tu ne penses pas aux choses de Dieu, mais à celles des {{gender:humains|hommes}}. »
fr.B: Jésus se retourna et dit à Pierre : « Passe derrière {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, Satan ! Tu es un obstacle sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} chemin. Tes pensées ne sont pas tournées vers les projets de Dieu, mais vers ceux des humains. »
fr.R: Jésus s’est retourné et a dit à Pierre : « Passe derrière {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, Satan ! Tu essaies de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} faire tomber. Tu ne penses pas comme Dieu pense. Tu penses comme pensent les gens. »

sw.L: Naye akageuka, akamwambia Petro, "Kaa nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, Shetani! Wewe ni kikwazo {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, kwa maana hufikiri mambo ya Mungu ila mambo ya binadamu."
sw.B: Yesu aligeuka, akamwambia Petro, "Kaa nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, Shetani! Wewe ni kikwazo katika njia {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Mawazo yako hayako kwenye makusudi ya Mungu, bali kwenye makusudi ya wanadamu."
sw.R: Yesu aligeuka, akamwambia Petro, "Kaa nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, Shetani! Unajaribu kunikwaza nianguke. Hufikiri jinsi Mungu anavyofikiri. Unafikiri jinsi wanadamu wanavyofikiri."

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} quay lại và nói với Phi-e-rơ: "Hãy lui ra sau {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, Sa-tan! Ngươi là hòn đá vấp chân cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì ngươi không nghĩ đến những việc của Đức Chúa Trời, nhưng đến những việc của loài người."

vi.R: Đức Giê-xu quay lại và nói với Phi-e-rơ: "Sa-tan, hãy lui ra sau {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}! Ngươi đang tìm cách làm cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vấp ngã. Ngươi đang suy nghĩ theo cách của loài người, chứ không theo cách của Đức Chúa Trời."

am.L: እርሱ ግን ዘወር ብሎ ጴጥሮስን አለው፦ «ሰይጣን ሆይ፣ ከኋላዬ ሂድ፤ ለእኔ ማሰናከያ ነህ፤ የእግዚአብሔርን ነገር አታስብምና፣ የሰዎችን ነገር እንጂ።»

decisions.choice: Satan: Peter speaks as Satan did, tempting Jesus away from the way of suffering
decisions.reason: In 4:8-10 Satan offered Jesus the kingdoms of the world without the cross, and Jesus said, "Go away, Satan." Peter's words make the same offer.

decisions.choice: get behind me: out of my way, and back to a follower's place
decisions.reason: The words are close to 4:10, but "behind me" is the same phrase as "come after me" in 16:24. Peter is to stop blocking the way and follow.

decisions.choice: stumbling block: something that trips and makes someone fall
decisions.reason: The word means a trap or an obstacle in the path. Peter's words would lead Jesus to turn from God's will.

decisions.choice: think the things of God: have God's purposes in mind
decisions.reason: The verb means to set the mind on something. Peter judges by human standards, not God's.

decisions.choice: trying to make me fall
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general.

decisions.choice: Ponte detrás de mí
decisions.reason: The words send Peter out of Jesus's way and back to a follower's place behind him (meaning decision m2, uncertain). "Ponte detrás de mí" keeps both; "quítate de delante" and "apártate" keep only the first.

decisions.choice: Va derrière moi (L), Passe derrière moi (B, R); une pierre d’achoppement (L), un obstacle sur mon chemin (B)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 8:33: "derrière moi" keeps the follower's place behind Jesus (m2) and the link with "venir derrière moi" in 16:24 at Literal. "Pierre d’achoppement" is the French expression for a stone that trips someone (m3), and it lets Literal keep the echo of the "pierre" of 16:18; "scandale" now means only an outrage.

decisions.choice: Kaa nyuma yangu
decisions.reason: The words send Peter out of Jesus's way and back to a follower's place behind him (meaning decision m2, uncertain). "Kaa nyuma yangu" (take your place behind me) keeps both; "ondoka mbele yangu" keeps only the first.

decisions.choice: "ngươi" for "you" in the rebuke
decisions.reason: As in Mark 8:33: Jesus addresses Peter as Satan, so the warm "con" would clash; "ngươi" is the form for speaking to an adversary. A reviewer may prefer another form.

decisions.choice: "hòn đá vấp chân" (L); "hòn đá cản đường" (B); "làm cho Ta vấp ngã" (R)
decisions.reason: Something that trips and makes one fall (meaning decision); each level keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: "내 뒤로 가라" (L), "내 뒤로 물러서라" (B), "내 뒤로 물러가거라" (R); "사탄"; "걸림돌" (L, B), "나를 넘어지게 하려고 한다" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 8:33, every level keeps "behind me", the place of a follower (meaning decision); "사탄" for satanas as settled. "걸림돌" is the everyday word for something that trips a person (meaning decision); "사람들" takes no gender span.

decisions.choice: "ማሰናከያ" (something that makes one stumble)
decisions.reason: "ማሰናከያ" comes from the verb "ማሰናከል", to make someone stumble and fall, which is the picture in the Greek; "እንቅፋት" is only something in the way. Readable uses the verb itself.
